# 2 Baruch Chapter 42 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Third Fast and Vision

---

**1** He answered me: "I'll explain these things to you as well.

**2** Those who were neither righteous nor wicked but lived somewhere in between — they are the ones who were plagued with troubles during their lives and endured suffering, even though they never fully served the wicked and never fully walked the paths of the just. They will be destroyed.

**3** Those who walked through this world with no righteousness in them, loving falsehood and ignoring the law of the Mighty One — they will be seized in the judgment. They will find no recognition.

**4** But those who truly loved the law and never lived with divided hearts about their faith — they are the ones who will inherit the world that will never pass away.

**5** And those whom the law separates out from among the mixed — they will be counted with the righteous.

**6** For the law itself will be the judge on that day. It will divide the just from the unjust, placing the righteous on the right hand and the wicked on the left.

**7** And that is my answer to your question."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. The law as final judge is a profound idea in 2 Baruch — Torah is not merely a guide but the eschatological criterion. The right/left separation (v.6) is one of the most striking images in the book.*
